lesson_title: Valley Climates: The Bathtub of Cold Air
hook_text: Why do vineyards grow HALFWAY up the mountain — never at the bottom? Cold air has a secret.
clip_script: On a clear night the slopes lose their heat fast, radiating it out to the stars. The air lying against them goes cold, and cold air is heavy air — it does not float, it flows, downhill, like water. All night, thin sheets of cold air dribble down both walls into the bottom of the valley. The valley floor is the bathtub: cold air from both walls pours in like water from two taps, and by three in the morning the tub is full. Frost whitens the bottom — while the warm shelf partway up the slope, the thermal belt, stays frost-free. That shelf is where the money grows.
visual_style: Night-time valley cross-section animation: glowing blue air sliding down both slopes into a filling bathtub on the floor, frost crystallising at the bottom while an orange thermal-belt band lights up mid-slope with rows of vines.
pacing: Slow pour as the tub fills, freeze-frame on the frost, warm reveal of the thermal belt.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and never mix up anabatic and katabatic again.
